title: The Sacred Mosque
hookLine: the mosque around the Ka'ba in Mecca

lines: A COMPASS APP, A CEILING ARROW.
cards: Somewhere in the house there's a phone with a little compass app, or a sticker on a hotel ceiling with an arrow, or a grandmother who just knows: that way. Every one of those arrows points to the same place.

Follow any of them far enough, over oceans and deserts, and you arrive at a great open courtyard in Mecca, white marble underfoot, colonnades all around, and in the middle a cube draped in black cloth, with crowds circling it day and night.
The building around that cube has a name. Today's word: Masjid al-Haram.

teach.b: Masjid al-Haram means the Sacred Mosque: the mosque around the Ka'ba. Pickthall renders it the Inviolable Place of Worship, a place set apart, where fighting is forbidden and pilgrims come in peace.
The Qur'an gives it a striking title: "Lo! the first Sanctuary appointed for mankind was that at Becca, a blessed place, a guidance to the peoples." Becca is understood as Mecca.
The Qur'an also tells how Abraham and his son Ishmael raised the foundations of the House, and prayed that God accept it from them. Then a turning point.
For a time in Medina, the reports say, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, and his companions prayed facing Jerusalem.
Then a verse came: "So turn thy face toward the Inviolable Place of Worship."
From that day, it has been the qibla, the direction of prayer, for Muslims everywhere: from a mosque in Senegal to a hospital prayer room in Seattle to a hiker on a mountain with a compass.
A hadith in Bukhari names three mosques worth setting out on a journey to visit: this one, the Prophet's Mosque in Medina, and al-Aqsa in Jerusalem. This one is today; the other two come next.
The Sacred Mosque is far from Senegal and Seattle, yet in a sense it is present in any prayer room set out to face it.
The first house, still at the center.

how: Muslims face the Ka'ba in the Sacred Mosque in Mecca for every prayer, using a mosque's prayer niche, a compass or a qibla app to find the direction, and pilgrims circle the Ka'ba within its courtyard during Hajj and Umrah.

Qur'an 3:96: "the first Sanctuary appointed for mankind was that at Becca."

games.q: you're praying in Medina with the Prophet's companions, facing Jerusalem, when a new verse is recited. which way do you face now?
o: toward the Inviolable Place of Worship in Mecca.
games.why: Qur'an 2:144: "So turn thy face toward the Inviolable Place of Worship." from then on, that is the qibla.

practice: If you have a phone, open a compass or qibla app and find the direction of Mecca from where you are, or guess roughly, and turn your chair or your body that way.
Notice that right now people in other rooms and other countries face the same point from every side, like spokes of a wheel.
If you pray, you can pray facing it in the way you know; if not, sit facing it and let the picture of that courtyard rest in your mind.

wordCard.voice: Masjid al-Haram. The Sacred Mosque around the Ka'ba in Mecca, the direction of every Muslim prayer. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: the first house. Every qibla arrow, anywhere, points to it. See you in Medina tomorrow.
